procedure_followed: E2_EXECUTION_DEVIATION.md section 13 -- a world whose OWN computation repeatedly triggers host-level memory kills is routed around and given an isolated supervisor writing to a SEPARATE output directory, so its failures cannot block or interleave with anything else.
why_this_is_a_determination_and_not_an_a: Section 13 required repeated evidence before declaring a world poison (it took 76 consecutive failed attempts there). This determination rests on FOUR independent OOM kills of the same world, across two different scheduling regimes, with a reproducible terminal footprint.

evidence.attempt: original run, co-scheduled with 11 other shards
evidence.headroom_available_gib: ~34 (47 total minus ~12.8 held by 11 sibling workers)
evidence.outcome: kernel global OOM kill; systemd then tore down the whole shared tmux scope, taking 11 healthy shards with it

evidence.attempt: Stage B attempt 1/3, ALONE on the host
evidence.outcome: kernel global OOM kill; exit code 137; ZERO collateral damage

evidence.attempt: Stage B attempt 2/3, ALONE on the host
evidence.outcome: kernel global OOM kill; exit code 137

evidence.attempt: Stage B attempt 3/3, ALONE on the host
evidence.outcome: kernel global OOM kill; exit code 137; supervisor exhausted its budget

conclusion_growth_is_unbounded.argument: Given ~34 GiB of headroom it died at 33.4 GiB. Given ~46 GiB it died at 47.7 GiB. Its demand expands to consume whatever is available and still exceeds the entire machine.
conclusion_growth_is_unbounded.reproducibility: The three isolated attempts terminated at 47,715,500 / 47,712,596 / 47,531,992 kB anon-RSS -- a spread of 0.4%. That is deterministic memory growth of the same computation, not noise or load sensitivity.
conclusion_growth_is_unbounded.corollary_for_worker_count: Reducing the frozen worker count would NOT have prevented the original failure, only delayed it. This retroactively confirms the results-blind decision recorded in RESUME_ENGINEERING_DECISION.json to retain 12 workers, which was made before any of this evidence existed.

no_partial_scientific_state.why: e2_run_shard_lazy.py writes candidate rows and then the world row only AFTER _run_one_world returns. Every attempt died inside the computation, so nothing was ever committed. Consistent with the Phase 2 audit, which found 0 orphan candidate rows.
no_partial_scientific_state.consequence: there is nothing to isolate, quarantine or delete -- the world simply has no record

isolation_worked.claim: The remediation recorded in RESUME_ENGINEERING_DECISION.json is empirically validated.
isolation_worked.before: 1 kernel OOM kill on 2026-08-18T03:11:34Z destroyed 12 shard units (1 killed by the kernel, 11 by systemd DefaultOOMPolicy=stop on the shared tmux scope).
isolation_worked.after: 3 kernel OOM kills on 2026-08-18T06:23-06:46 destroyed 0 units other than the one being killed. e2a-progress.service and e2a-watchdog.service remained running throughout, and the 539-world main corpus was untouched.
isolation_worked.mechanism: per-shard transient systemd user units with OOMPolicy=continue in app.slice

handling_under_the_frozen_routing_rule.authority: routing_lock.evaluate_gate2's own docstring: r_remaining 'includes any quarantined-but-unresolved world, e.g. the poison world ... since its eventual stage is exactly as unknown as any other outstanding world's, and must be treated as adversarially unknown, never assumed'
handling_under_the_frozen_routing_rule.consequence: the seal reports 539 completed + 1 unresolved = 540 accounted for, and Gate 2 branch 1 can still lock if and only if B_n > A_n + 1 AND B_n > C_n + D_n + 1

not_claimed: That the root cause inside the computation is identified. The growth is in the shard parent process, not the classify worker, and is consistent with unbounded sympy/equivalence work on this world's expressions -- but no specific defect is named here, because none was proven.
That this world would fail on any other host. It is a determination about THIS frozen environment on THIS x86_64 host, which is the only environment the authorization permits.
That the world's scientific outcome is known or can be inferred. It is unresolved, and is treated as adversarially unknown.
